title: Many Travelers Become Different People on Vacation
paragraphs: At home, you might be a doctor or a teacher. You might be a brother or a mother; a swimmer or a soccer player; a colleague or a regular at your local café.
But when you're abroad, you're often just a traveler.
Research suggests that many people feel that they become a different person when they travel — and some do so deliberately.

An astrology app called Hint recently surveyed almost 15,000 travelers from different parts of the world. It found that 61% of them deliberately behave differently when they're in another country, compared to how they would behave at home.
And nearly half of participants said they had knowingly done something while traveling that they would not have done at home.
But it's not just behaviors — some people find that their personality changes when they travel too.
A 2025 survey by Faye Travel Insurance found that many Americans think they're more likely to embrace their fun side when they travel.
Forty percent said they become more adventurous eaters, and a similar percentage believe they're friendlier when they travel.
There could be a few reasons for this. Removing the stresses and routines of everyday life might help people relax in ways they can't at home.
But psychologists suggest something deeper may be happening: travel changes the context in which we see ourselves.
A 2026 study suggests that people's views of themselves can change between "home" and "vacation" settings.
The researchers said that unfamiliar surroundings can temporarily make a "vacation identity" more prominent, while people's "home identity" goes quiet.
Travel can also give people something they rarely have at home: anonymity.
At home, our behavior exists within a social history. The people around us know what we are normally like, and we know that we'll probably see them again.
Abroad, that history often disappears — and because people are less likely to see other travelers again, they might lower some of their usual inhibitions.
